newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close slightly lower, banks up.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close slightly lower, banks up.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks edged to a slightly lower close on Monday, but brokers said the index would have been harder hit without the strength in finance counters, particularly HSBC Holdings.
"A large part of this (activity today) is Hongkong Bank," said David Williamson, director at W.I. Carr.

The Hang Seng Index slipped 16.96 points, or 0.12 percent, to 13,643.54, well off the opening high of 13,860.88. Turnover was HK$7.63 billion, compared with HK$7.25 billion on February 5, the last session before the Chinese New Year holiday.
Finance counters, chiefly HSBC Holdings, led the market. The international banking giant closed HK$5.50 higher at HK$189.50, after setting an all-time high of HK$191.50.
Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.25 to HK$93.50.
Brokers said HSBC's gains were due in part to the strength of the U.S. dollar, which would boost the bank's earnings report in sterling.
"The bank's results will be out on March 3, and I expect the share to be strong in advance of that," said Robin Fox of Nomura Research Institute.
Williamson said he expected to see HSBC break through HK$200.
The market opened high but lacked momentum or real buying interest, despite Wall Street's bullish performance on Friday, said Andrew To, dealing director at OSK Asia Securities.
"What we saw today was a negative, single-day reversal," To said.
The Dow put on 82.74 points to 6,855.80, due chiefly to a favourable U.S. unemployment report for January.
"This (intra-day) reversal is not very bearish, but it does further confirm technical resistance at 13,800 to 14,000," said To.
Brokers also said they were concerned about the trend in Hang Seng futures, where the spot month had been trading on average at a discount to the cash market since Christmas.
The Hang Seng Index futures contract for February closed 60 points lower at 13,560, an 83-point discount to the cash market. March closed 45 points down at 13,580.
The property sector was the worst performing.
Sun Hung Kai Properties slipped HK$2.00 to HK$91.00 and Henderson Land eased HK$2.00 to HK$71.50.
Cheung Kong lost HK$1.50 to HK$74.25.
